issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 21/08/26

✅ Implementation: Recommendations — Popular Posts Feed

Route

GET /recommendations/posts/popular?window=&page=&limit=&lat=&lng=&radius=
Authorization: <JWT token>

Changes

  • Added Action/V1/Recommendations/Shared.go: request-param parsing/validation (parseRecoParams), the shared response envelope builder (buildEnvelope, gated on RECO_DEBUG), the Redis exclusion-list loader (loadRedisStrings, same base64+JSON idiom as Action/V2/Posts/DetailPost.go), the KYC signal loader (loadUserKYC, reading user_detail.place_interests/usage_intent), a local parseInterests (handles the double-encoded JSON case seen in user_detail.place_interests) and envFloat helper, window↔column mapping (velocityColumn, nextWindow), and the popularity ORDER BY expression builder (popularOrderExpr).
  • Added Action/V1/Recommendations/PopularPosts.go: the #511 handler itself (flow below).
  • Added Controllers/V1/RecommendationsControllers.go and Routes/V1/RecommendationsRoutes.go; registered a new recommendations route group in Routes/V1/Routes.go next to the existing bookmarks group.
  • Did not modify any existing endpoint, model, or response shape.
  • The scoring math (velocity/quality) itself is computed by a separate cron in the sibling repo panorra-api-new (checked out locally as panorra-api-go-new/), not this repo — see that repo's docs/tasks/2026-08-21/update_recommendation_scores_cron.md. This endpoint only reads the posts.score_velocity_* / posts.score_quality columns that cron writes.

Dependency: the posts.score_velocity_* columns and the interest_category_map table are created by panorra-api-new's migration (PR #479). Until that lands, every request falls through to the popular_alltime tier and the interest boost never fires. Merge order is #479 first, then this PR.

Data Flow

  1. Resolve role/encrypt from auth middleware locals; reject with 401 if neither "user" nor "viewer".
  2. Parse and validate query params (page/limit/window/lat/lng/radius) via parseRecoParams; 400 on invalid input.
  3. For role == "user", re-check the account with UserFunctions.UserDatas(c, encrypt) and return 401 if it reports status: "error" — the same check Action/V1/Posts/MostPopularPostFeed.go does. A structurally valid JWT belonging to a deleted or deactivated user must not get a feed. Viewers skip this, as they have no account record to check.
  4. Load exclusion lists: deactivated users (always) and, for authenticated users, blocked users + blocked posts (existing Redis keys, same as every other Explore feed handler).
  5. For authenticated users only: load KYC place_interests + usage_intent from user_detail, then resolve interest keys to category IDs via interest_category_map. If any categories match, remember them for the ranking boost and for debug.usedInterests.
  6. Build a filtered GORM query (views_timeline_post joined to posts) shared by both the Count and the Scan call, so the pagination total stays consistent with the returned page.
  7. Fallback chain, starting at the requested window:
    1. Try the requested window's velocity column (score_velocity_24h/_7d/_30d), requiring it to be > 0.
    2. If zero rows match, widen to the next coarser window (24h → 7d → 30d) and retry.
    3. If even 30d has no rows anywhere (e.g. the cron has never run yet, or hasn't reached this post yet), fall back to the existing all-time score_mostpopular column with no velocity requirement — this tier always has rows once posts.score_mostpopular is populated.
    4. Whichever tier first returns rows sets strategy (popular_<window> / popular_alltime, or the popular_personalized_* variant when an interest boost is in the ORDER BY) and, if the tier isn't the one requested, sets debug.fallbackReason.
    5. A tier whose Count or Scan returns a DB error is logged and reported as empty, so the chain widens instead of returning 500. The log line is the only unconditional signal — debug.fallbackReason is gated behind RECO_DEBUG, so without it a missing migration would be indistinguishable from a genuinely empty tier. A failed Scan reports total = 0 as well, so the response never pairs a non-zero total with an empty data array.
  8. Rank matching rows by popularOrderExpr, with slug as a stable tiebreaker, and paginate by offset/limit:
    • No interest boost (viewers, and users without matching KYC categories — likely the majority): order by the bare score column. x/(x+k) is strictly increasing for x ≥ 0, k > 0, so normalizing cannot change the ordering on its own; skipping it also keeps an index on score_velocity_* usable.
    • With an interest boost: order by the normalized score p.<col> / (p.<col> + RECO_NORM_K) plus a flat +0.1 for a category match. Normalization matters here, because it puts the raw score on a 0..1 scale the flat bonus can meaningfully compete with. RECO_NORM_K falls back to the default 100 if configured ≤ 0, since k = 0 would evaluate 0/(0+0) for a zero-score row and Postgres raises division_by_zero, failing the whole query.
  9. Build the response exactly the way Action/V2/Posts/DetailPost.go does: the PRD recommendation envelope (data/total/page/limit/strategy, plus debug only when RECO_DEBUG=true) gains valid/version/messages and goes inside the repo's standard {statusCode: 200, data: …} wrapper.
  10. If the request carries ec: true, encrypt that same object: derive the key from lastLogin + encrypt via Functions.KeyEncrypt, pass []interface{}{secret, lastLogin, 0, response} to Functions.EncryptResult, and return {messages, cry, ls} — plus e4 for viewers. Because the encrypted payload is the unmodified cleartext response, a decrypted response and a plain one are identical. lastLogin comes from the UserFunctions.UserDatas call already made for the auth check, read with a checked type assertion; viewers have no account record, so they keep the request-time value.
  11. Return 200.

Known gaps

  • lat/lng/radius are validated but do not affect ranking yet — they are in the public contract ahead of the Phase 2 places work, flagged with a ponytail: comment in the handler.
  • Up to 6 queries per request (3 tiers × Count + Scan), each an expression ORDER BY over views_timeline_post JOIN posts. Acceptable while the tiers short-circuit on the first non-empty one; revisit if the all-time fallback becomes the common path.

Git

Branch feat/personalized-explore-score, pushed as PR #517.

Endpoint

GET /recommendations/posts/popular

Background

Part of the personalized-explore epic (#506, PRD docs/prd/2026-08-21-personalized-explore-prd.md). Existing Explore feeds (posts/most-popular-post-feed, etc.) rank purely by all-time score_mostpopular. This endpoint implements issue #511 and is the terminal fallback for every other Phase 2/3 recommendation endpoint: it ranks by windowed engagement velocity (24h/7d/30d, computed by a new cron in panorra-api-go-new) with an optional KYC-interest-category boost, and falls back to coarser windows and finally to all-time popularity when no velocity data exists yet.

Scope

  • Query params: window (24h|7d|30d, default 7d), page (default 1), limit (default 12, max 50), lat/lng/radius (accepted, not yet applied to ranking — reserved for the Phase 2 places work).
  • Auth: existing role check (user/viewer); 401 otherwise.
  • Filtering: excludes deactivated users, blocked users, blocked posts (existing Redis idioms), non-public visibility, and video360 post type — identical filter set to posts/most-popular-post-feed.
  • Ranking: normalized velocity for the requested window (score / (score + K), K env-tunable via RECO_NORM_K) plus a flat +0.1 boost when the post's category matches one of the logged-in user's KYC interests (resolved via interest_category_map).
  • Fallback chain: requested window → next coarser window → all-time score_mostpopular. The first tier with any matching rows wins.
  • Response: shared envelope {data, total, page, limit, strategy, debug?}. strategy communicates which tier served the response (e.g. popular_7d, popular_personalized_24h, popular_alltime). debug (interest keys used, intent, fallback reason) is included only when env RECO_DEBUG=true.
  • Does not modify any existing endpoint, model, or response shape.

Request

GET /recommendations/posts/popular?window=7d&page=1&limit=12
Authorization: <JWT token>

Response Fields

{
  "data": [ /* Models.ListPostsTimelineFeed rows — same shape as posts/most-popular-post-feed */ ],
  "total": 128,
  "page": 1,
  "limit": 12,
  "strategy": "popular_personalized_7d",
  "debug": {
    "usedInterests": ["nature_scenery"],
    "usedIntent": "explore_virtually",
    "fallbackReason": ""
  }
}

debug is omitted entirely unless RECO_DEBUG=true.
